items.title: Russian warship struck by suspected Ukrainian drones at Libya naval base
items.summary: Libyan officials say a suspected Ukrainian drone strike has hit a Russian warship at a naval base in Libya.
items.t: Russian warship struck by suspected Ukrainian drones at Libya naval base

items.title: Le Pen denies receiving leaked information from French interior ministry official
items.summary: French far-right leader Marine Le Pen on Sunday said she did not receive, nor ask for, confidential information on an investigation into her party from a senior interior ministry official. She however could not say if other party members had benefited from the leaks. Hugues Moutouh, the civil servant under suspicion, has denied the allegations and asked to be relieved of his duties pending a probe.
items.t: Le Pen denies receiving leaked information from French interior ministry official

items.title: Lebanese villagers return to wrecked homes as the Israeli army pulls back
items.summary:
In a pilot project in a village in southern Lebanon, Israeli forces have left and the Lebanese army moved it. But villagers who return find their houses wrecked.

(Image credit: Mohammed Yassine for NPR)
items.t: Lebanese villagers return to wrecked homes as the Israeli army pulls back

items.title: Ligue 1: PSG extend winning run at Nice (3-2) but lose Désiré Doué to injury
items.summary: A bittersweet victory for PSG at Nice on Saturday evening. The Parisians strengthened their grip on top spot in Ligue 1, but lost Désiré Doué for several months after the forward suffered a serious knee injury.
items.t: Ligue 1: PSG extend winning run at Nice (3-2) but lose Désiré Doué to injury

items.title: Blast on Russian ship in Benghazi a suspected drone attack, say Libyan authorities
items.summary:
No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia

An explosion on a Russian ship docked at the naval base in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya’s eastern-based government has said.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the suspected strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the frontlines.

Continue reading...
items.t: Blast on Russian ship in Benghazi a suspected drone attack, say Libyan authorities

items.title: Climate change talks fall apart in final hours over fossil fuels
items.summary:
Some 200 countries gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the annual climate negotiations. Countries failed to reach an agreement over fossil fuels - the primary driver of global warming.

(Image credit: Khalil Hamra)
items.t: International climate talks end in disappointment

items.title: Trump says he wants "permanent" deal with Iran
items.summary: Despite rising tension, President Trump told an Israeli outlet he may not make a decision on his next move in the Iran war until 2027.
items.t: Trump insists he's "not rushing to make any decisions on Iran"

items.title: West Bank attacks: Opposition leader Eisenkot decries "Jewish terrorism"
items.summary: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were set on fire in three villages in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers were deployed to the area following the attacks, which local residents said were carried out by Israeli settlers. Gadi Eisenkot, a rival of outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, condemned the acts on X, describing them as “Jewish terrorism”. Antonia Kerrigan reports.
items.t: West Bank attacks: Opposition leader Eisenkot decries "Jewish terrorism"

items.title: Russian strike kills 2 in Kyiv
items.summary: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in the village of Dymer, just north of Kyiv, on Sunday, killing at least two people and wounding four others. The morning strike destroyed a five-storey building, while rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child. At least 11 others are believed to remain trapped under the rubble.
items.t: Russian strike kills 2 in Kyiv

items.title: Cop31 climate talks break down as key deal rejected
items.summary:
EU, UK and some of developing world object to main text that ‘failed to meet the moment’ and did not mention fossil fuels

The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world rejected what they called an unacceptable deal on the future of the climate, which failed even to mention fossil fuels, in a dramatic finish to the Cop31 UN talks in Turkey.

The proposed deal “failed to meet the moment”, said Ireland’s environment minister, Darragh O’Brien, speaking for the EU. “We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required. [It] does not even mention fossil fuels.”

Continue reading...
items.t: Cop31 climate talks break down as key deal rejected

items.title: U.N. climate summit ends without deal after contentious fossil fuel debate
items.summary: COP31, the latest installment of the United Nations' annual climate conference, ended Sunday without a final agreement after days of contentious talks collapsed.
items.t: U.N. climate summit ends without deal after contentious fossil fuel debate

items.title: The mythic origin of Chilean sea bass
items.summary: It's a fish that underwent a rebranding in the 1970s and went on to become one of the most popular seafood imports in the United States. But what is Chilean sea bass actually? Correspondent David Pogue looks into the story of a previously-unloved fish with an unfortunate name that became such a favorite of chefs and the public that it was overfished.
items.t: The mythic origin of Chilean sea bass

items.title: Sardinian pasta: Making the "Threads of God"
items.summary: In the rugged interior of Sardinia, a dedicated few still make a traditional form of pasta called su filindeu, or The Threads of God. Correspondent Seth Doane finds out what goes into making what is often called the rarest pasta on Earth.
items.t: Sardinian pasta: Making the "Threads of God"

items.title: The week in pictures: Xi hosts Trump and Putin, COP31 and new French protests
items.summary: From the unprecedented Shenzhen summit in China that saw President Xi Jinping host his US and Russian counterparts, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, to tough talks at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey and another week of French protests over the cost of living, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.
items.t: The week in pictures: Xi hosts Trump and Putin, COP31 and new French protests

items.title: "It can take years": Why the AI Riemann proof is far from settled
items.summary: AI claimed another major scalp in maths on Friday, as Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge published what he says is a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a Millennium Prize Problem, in 17 million lines of code that no human has read in full. Physicist Tony Padilla tells Tech 24 that verification could take years, and that Alpöge should share how he got there.
items.t: "It can take years": Why the AI Riemann proof is far from settled

items.title: Potty-mouthed MPs ranked as Australian parliament sets new swearing record
items.summary:
One serial sweary offender, Jacqui Lambie, says it wouldn’t be an Australian parliament ‘without a few swear words thrown in’

  • Want to get more charts in your inbox every fortnight? Sign up for The Crunch here

When Liberal MP Garth Hamilton stormed out of parliament in June, slamming his hands on his desk and calling out “fucking bullshit” the speaker of the house, Milton Dick, called it “a new low” in federal politics.

Dick may have been on to something.

Continue reading...
items.t: Potty-mouthed MPs ranked as Australian parliament sets new swearing record

items.title: Australia urged to wean off imported fossil fuels amid global supply shocks
items.summary:
Grattan Institute report calls on government to ‘seize’ opportunity to cap diesel tax credits, introduce EV subsidies for less wealthy’ and build ‘clean’ refineries

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Capping lucrative diesel tax handouts to big business, building new “clean” refineries and targeting electric vehicle subsidies to less wealthy people could save Australians thousands of dollars in fuel per year, according to a major new report calling on the government to reduce reliance on imported fossil fuels.

The Grattan Institute, one of the nation’s most respected thinktanks, has warned Australia imports too much of its fuel, and that the country must brace for more global supply shocks – like that from the war in Iran. Under a plan already attracting criticism from business groups, Grattan urged diesel handouts to mining and primary industries be curbed in favour of incentives for electric trucks and a huge expansion of the EV charging network.

Continue reading...
items.t: Australia urged to wean off imported fossil fuels amid global supply shocks

items.title: 11/22: Sunday Morning
items.summary: Jane Pauley hosts our annual Food Issue. Featured: Food debt; in-home restaurants; Sardinian pasta; chef Kwame Onwuachi; actor Tony Shalhoub; Sallie Ann Robinson on Gullah cuisine; Wisconsin's supper clubs; food for the outdoors; and stories behind Brussels sprouts, cottage cheese, and Chilean sea bass.
items.t: 11/22: Sunday Morning

items.title: Israel investigates West Bank fires
items.summary: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were vandalised and set on fire in four villages in the occupied West Bank, in attacks local activists say were carried out by Israeli settlers. Around eight vehicles were reportedly torched and racist slogans sprayed on walls, prompting Israeli soldiers and police to deploy to the area. The attacks come amid a surge in settler violence since the outbreak of the Gaza war in October 2023, with more than 1,100 Palestinians killed by Israeli soldiers or settlers in the West Bank since then, according to an AFP tally. They also follow recent sanctions announced by the UK and Australia against eight Israeli companies involved in settlement activity. France 24 correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky shares further details from Jerusalem.
items.t: Israel investigates West Bank fires

items.title: 🔴 COP31 ends without deal as EU rejects text for omitting mention of fossil fuels
items.summary: EU member states on Sunday objected to adopting an 11th-hour deal that omitted explicit references to fossil fuels, the bloc's presidency said. The issue remains a major point of contention at the summit,…
items.t: 🔴 COP31 ends without deal as EU rejects text for omitting mention of fossil fuels
items.lead: EU member states on Sunday objected to adopting an 11th-hour deal that omitted explicit references to fossil fuels, the bloc's presidency said. The issue remains a major point of contention at the summit,…

items.title: South Korean minister quits after AI cheating scandal engulfs university exams
items.summary:
Choi Kyo-jin says he ‘failed to prepare adequately’ for entrance exams following last-minute scramble to tighten measures

South Korea’s education minister has resigned after an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted in the lead-up to key university entrance exams last week.

The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday, when the top scorer in a national tax accountancy exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score, just four days before the crucial university entrance exam, known as the suneung.

Continue reading...
items.t: South Korea education minister resigns after AI cheating scandal engulfs university exams

items.title: Indonesia factory hit by deadly blaze: Three killed and 36 missing
items.summary: At least three people have been killed and dozens are missing after a fire broke out at a factory in Indonesia producing sweets and snack products. Fifteen people were rescued alive from the plant, while firefighters were still battling flames in several parts of the facility more than 12 hours after the blaze began. The cause of the fire remains unknown, but survivors said it started in a cooling unit on the third floor.
items.t: Indonesia factory hit by deadly blaze: Three killed and 36 missing

items.title: UK-EU food deal hailed by British firms: ‘We’re pretty aligned anyway’
items.summary:
Exporters welcome end in sight for Brexit checks – but are frustrated that implementation will take so long

British producers have broadly welcomed the UK’s deal with the EU, designed to remove the vast majority of physical checks on food, plants and animal products.

The sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) deal is expected to benefit Britain’s food exporters and will enable UK delicatessens and other small retailers to import European cheese and wine again, something that became economically unviable because of costly Brexit checks.

Continue reading...
items.t: UK-EU food deal hailed by British firms: ‘We’re pretty aligned anyway’

items.title: Former Italian police chief found dead
items.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has expressed shock following the death of a former national police chief, whose body was found on Saturday. He had been under investigation over an alleged cover-up in an inquiry into a bombing linked to organised crime in Sicily. Jennie Shin reports.
items.t: Former Italian police chief found dead

items.title: Princess of Wales opens up about cancer
items.summary: A new documentary titled Heal follows Britain’s Princess Catherine as she navigates life since her cancer diagnosis in 2024. The film tracks the 44-year-old as she attempts to climb the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours. In the trailer, she reflects on healing as a journey. Ophelie Jacobson reports.
items.t: Princess of Wales opens up about cancer

items.title: South Korea: AI cheating sparks exam security chaos
items.summary: South Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday following a major cheating scandal that erupted just ahead of the country’s university entrance exams. The controversy centred on the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam, who admitted to using a miniature camera and smartphone to secure a near-perfect result. Jack Pownall reports.
items.t: South Korea: AI cheating sparks exam security chaos

items.title: Europe sees new protests over rising costs, inequality and public services
items.summary: Sunday marks the third consecutive day of protests across Europe, following large demonstrations on Friday and smaller rallies on Saturday, from Portugal to France. The protests have largely focused on the rising cost of living and access to affordable housing. In France, demonstrations have now taken place for six weekends in a row. Ophelie Jacobson reports.
items.t: Europe sees new protests over rising costs, inequality and public services

items.title: English village votes to "leave UK"
items.summary: Residents of the small English village of Barnham voted on Saturday in a symbolic referendum to leave the UK, in protest against government plans to house 931 asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base – more than the village’s own population of 584. The vote follows a similar protest in another village in September, highlighting growing tensions over immigration across the country. Earlier this week, the leader of a far-right anti-immigration group was jailed, but supporters have vowed to keep the movement alive. Jack Pownall reports.
items.t: English village votes to "leave UK"

items.title: NATO faces sovereignty dilemma as militaries rely on private tech, AI
items.summary: NATO officials and defence experts gathered at the NATO Edge conference in Turkey this week to discuss how militaries can harness artificial intelligence and high tech without compromising control over sensitive data and defence capabilities.
items.t: NATO faces sovereignty dilemma as militaries rely on private tech, AI

items.title: China, ASEAN countries struggle over South China Sea code of conduct
items.summary: The Philippines wanted a South China Sea code of conduct in place by 2026. But persistent disagreements between China and ASEAN countries are slowing progress toward a deal.
items.t: China, ASEAN countries struggle over South China Sea code of conduct

items.title: Bank of England directors illegally profited from post-abolition enslavement in Cuba
items.summary:
New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people

• Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds

British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.

Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.

Continue reading...
items.t: Highly lucrative: Bank of England directors illegally profited from post-abolition enslavement in Cuba

items.title: Fire at confectionery factory in Indonesia leaves at least three dead and dozens missing
items.summary:
Relatives of the missing victims flocked to the factory’s entrance, seeking updates about their loved ones

A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta has killed three people with 36 remaining missing, an Indonesian rescue official says.

Drone footage showed large parts of the factory destroyed, with the roof collapsed in places and smoke still rising from the complex. Photos and videos shared by rescuers show officers entering the charred building in search of the missing victims on Sunday, with small fires still burning in some spots.

Continue reading...
items.t: Fire at confectionary factory in Indonesia leaves at least three dead and dozens missing

items.title: Live: Ukrainian rescuers search for survivors in rubble after Russian attack
items.summary: Ukrainian rescue teams on Sunday searched for survivors in the rubble of a collapsed residential building in Dymer, in the Kyiv region, after a Russian drone strike, which killed two people and wounded four others. Meanwhile, Finland warned the war was "spilling over" after a drone set fire to a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic Sea Saturday. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.
items.t: Live: Finland says war 'spilling over' after Baltic Sea drone strike on Russian cargo ship

items.title: Dozens missing as deadly fire hits Indonesian candy factory
items.summary: At least three people were killed in a devastating fire at a confectionery factory on Java. Officials said many more people remain unaccounted for, prompting fears of a much larger tragedy.
items.t: Dozens missing as deadly fire hits Indonesian candy factory

items.title: ‘Serious error of judgment’: outrage over military AI event at Berlin arts complex
items.summary:
Kraftwerk Berlin, part of same development as techno club Tresor, transformed into ‘war room’ for arms firm event

With their cavernous post-industrial venues, teeth-grinding four-by-four beats and bouncers that look like Blade Runner extras, Berlin’s nightclubs trade on a reputation for bleakness. A recent event at one of the city’s most legendary clubland institutions, however, has proven too dystopian even for seasoned techno-heads.

On 11 November, the Kraftwerk Berlin arts complex had its central hall transformed into what visitors described as something resembling a war room, with maps and aerial footage projected on to concrete walls, drones hanging from the ceiling, and guards in flak jackets patrolling the premises with sniffer dogs.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Serious error of judgment’: outrage over military AI event at Berlin arts complex

items.title: Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations
items.summary:
As nationalist, Eurosceptic parties surge in four of the bloc’s biggest member states, the coming year’s polls could test its resilience like never before

In late 1998, Tony Blair was prime minister of Britain, Lionel Jospin was prime minister of France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany. The EU had 15 member states and pro-European, centre-left parties were in power – either alone or in coalitions – in all but two of them.

Brisk economic growth was lifting living standards. Eastward enlargement was under way. In Washington, Bill Clinton was pursuing the same brand of “third way” centrism as a middle path between free-market capitalism and traditional socialism. The EU felt like it had the tide of history behind it.

Continue reading...
items.t: Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations

items.title: Police say man whose body lay undiscovered in Sydney bushland for 12 days was killed in suspected hit-and-run
items.summary:
Joshua Howard, 31, is believed to have been struck by a car and thrown over the guardrail as he was walking home from a party in Rouse Hill

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The twin brother of a man whose body lay undiscovered for 12 days after he was killed in a suspected hit and run in Sydney says it has left him feeling like half a person.

Joshua Howard was last seen at a bus interchange in Parramatta, in western Sydney, about 10pm on 7 November.

Continue reading...
items.t: Police say man whose body lay undiscovered in Sydney bushland for 12 days was killed in suspected hit-and-run

items.title: South Korean education minister resigns over AI-driven exam cheating scandal
items.summary: South Korea Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned Sunday over an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted days before the high-stakes Suneung university entrance exam. The Suneung concluded "without any major incidents" last week, Choi said, but he admitted to a failure to "prepare adequately in advance".
items.t: South Korean education minister resigns over AI-driven exam cheating scandal

items.title: Bahrain accuses Iran of striking industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
items.summary: Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial site on Saturday evening, as two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran reported shooting down a US drone amid stalled efforts to end the war.
items.t: Bahrain accuses Iran of striking industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz

items.title: Man found dead on Flinders Island believed to have been shot by officer, police say
items.summary:
The sergeant, who was shot, fired his weapon a number of times after alleged ‘targeted’ attack outside island’s police station

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A police officer who was shot outside a remote Tasmanian police station is alleged to have shot and killed his attacker in response to what authorities believe was a “targeted” incident.

Tasmania police deputy commissioner, Jonathan Higgins, said the sergeant Michael Preshaw had just come off shift at Whitemark police station on Flinders Island, which is north-east of the Tasmanian mainland. He had parked and gotten out of his police vehicle when he was shot at about 9.45pm on Saturday, Higgins told reporters on Sunday.

Continue reading...
items.t: Man found dead on Flinders Island linked to shooting of police officer, Tasmanian authorities say

items.title: Victorian Greens win injunction over how-to-vote cards mimicking party’s branding but preferencing it last
items.summary:
Exclusive: Independent candidate Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s cards instructed people to vote in a way that would benefit Liberal party

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian Greens have won a supreme court injunction to stop an independent candidate from handing out how to vote cards that mimic their branding and urge people to preference it last.

The decision has been welcomed by the party’s leader, Ellen Sandell, who said the flyers distributed by people wearing the exact same colour shirts as genuine Greens volunteers had already misled voters.

Continue reading...
items.t: Victorian Greens win injunction over how-to-vote cards mimicking party’s branding but preferencing it last

items.title: Athlete swims Strait of Hormuz to highlight Iran war's wildlife toll
items.summary: British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh has swum the Strait of Hormuz to highlight environmental threats during ongoing conflict.
items.t: Athlete swims Strait of Hormuz to highlight Iran war's wildlife toll

items.title: Violence breaks out in Mexico after capture of drug kingpin wanted by FBI
items.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores is allegedly the leader of a cartel responsible for drug distribution and importation.
items.t: Violence breaks out in Mexico after capture of drug kingpin wanted by FBI

items.title: EU-Indonesia agreement sees the light after ten years of negotiations
items.summary: The European Union and Indonesia have signed a major trade deal, ten years after talks began.The agreement removes almost all tariffs between the EU and Southeast Asia's biggest economy: 98.5 per cent of them. For Europe, it means access to a market of 280 million people and a steadier supply of nickel for batteries. For Indonesia, easier exports of palm oil, textiles and footwear, and it arrives just before its current EU trade preferences end on the 1st of January. To discuss the deal Airlangga Hartarto, Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs in Indonesia joined us on the programme.
items.t: EU-Indonesia agreement sees the light after ten years of negotiations

items.title: What did Xi Jinping get from the bear hug with Trump at the Shenzhen summit?
items.summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Robert Daly, director of the program on US China relations at University of Maryland's School of Public Policy, about President Trump's trip to China this week.
items.t: What did Xi Jinping get from the bear hug with Trump at the Shenzhen summit?

items.title: Highlights and challenges from covering an historic month in South America
items.summary: NPR's South America Correspondent discusses her work covering an historic election upset and a papal visit.
items.t: Highlights and challenges from covering an historic month in South America

items.title: A grieving family in Lebanon returns to their village
items.summary: In Southern Lebanon, the Army is taking over after Israeli forces withdraw. One grieving family returns to their village to find almost everything in their house destroyed.
items.t: A grieving family in Lebanon returns to their village

items.title: Princess Kate reflects on healing in new documentary: "Cancer does change you"
items.summary: The princess reflects on her cancer journey in the documentary and speaks to others about their experiences.
items.t: Princess Kate reflects on healing in new documentary: "Cancer does change you"

items.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for ‘marathon’ Israeli coalition talks
items.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has invited caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party for coalition talks, his centrist Yashar party said Saturday. The "marathon series of talks" starts Sunday, the party said, adding that the move reflected a commitment to form "the broadest possible government" after the October election failed to deliver an outright winner.
items.t: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for ‘marathon’ Israeli coalition talks

items.title: France’s sixth consecutive Saturday of protests draws lower turnout
items.summary: Turnout ⁠was down ​at largely peaceful demonstrations across France on the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests ​over the cost of living, with the interior ministry putting the figure at 82,500 across the country. Organisers said 150,000 people participated in the nationwide protests, down from their 200,000 figure last week.
items.t: France’s sixth consecutive Saturday of protests draw lower turnout

items.title: 'Worst Ever' COP Summit?
items.summary:
Is this the worst COP summit on record?

With limited political leadership, no official US delegation and mounting frustration over bureaucratic delays, questions are being raised about the effectiveness of the climate negotiations.

Juan Carlos Beldsoe, a former White House climate adviser under Bill Clinton, described the process as labyrinthine and ultimately dispiriting.

France 24's Gavin Lee speaks with climate advocate and six-time COP delegate, Henna Hundal about what this means for the future of global climate action.
items.t: 'Worst Ever' COP Summit?

items.title: Russia attacks Zelensky's hometown, Ukraine reaffirms wish to join NATO
items.summary: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO, following proposals to provide Kyiv with security guarantees similar to those of the military alliance.
items.t: Russia attacks Zelensky's hometown, Ukraine reaffirms wish to join NATO

items.title: Russia launches ballistic missile attack on Zelensky's hometown in central Ukraine
items.summary: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv.
items.t: Russia launches ballistic missile attack on Zelensky's hometown in central Ukraine

items.title: Cartel leader captured in northern Mexico in a bloody firefight that left 11 dead
items.summary:
Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, better known as "El Chapo Isidro," was one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives. His arrest in northwest Mexico on Saturday has sparked violence in the region.

(Image credit: Claudia Rosel)
items.t: Mexico detains top cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro,' setting off violence

items.title: Alleged Mexican drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ arrested in special forces raid
items.summary:
Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was one of FBI’s most wanted fugitives and evaded capture for more than a decade

The Mexican military captured one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives during a special forces raid in the Mexican state of Sinaloa on Friday night.

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was arrested along with two other alleged leaders of his gang after a gun battle that triggered widespread panic in the city of Guasave.

Continue reading...
items.t: Alleged Mexican drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ arrested in special forces raid

items.title: Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace
items.summary: Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.
items.t: Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace

items.title: Families frustrated with Pentagon probe of deadly drone strike
items.summary: The Pentagon is preparing to release findings of its investigation into the attack that killed six U.S. soldiers in Kuwait early in the Iran war.
items.t: Families frustrated with Pentagon probe of deadly drone strike

items.title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
items.summary:
Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’

Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections.

Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.

Continue reading...
items.t: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse

items.title: The mysterious migration of monarch butterflies
items.summary: Photographer Jaime Rojo says an iconic 1976 National Geographic cover showing monarch butterflies captivated him, inspiring his own photography. Rojo's new book "Monarchs" chronicles ways we can help save this beloved insect.
items.t: The mysterious migration of monarch butterflies

items.title: Princess Kate announces she's in remission from cancer
items.summary: Princess Kate made the announcement on social media after visiting the London hospital where she received treatment.
items.t: Princess Kate announces she's in remission from cancer

items.title: How China gets access to American AI chips
items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned from his role as Nvidia CEO following an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy. After the Nvidia scandal, China's access to American-made technology and advanced AI chips came under renewed scrutiny. Ramy Inocencio traveled to Southeast Asia to learn more about Chinese usage of American chips.
items.t: How China gets access to American AI chips

items.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
items.summary: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.
items.t: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal

items.title: Trump defends Putin after trilateral with Xi
items.summary: President Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin appeared to make little progress in their trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China.
items.t: Trump defends Putin after trilateral with Xi

items.title: New EU budget proposal aims at tax gobal tech giants
items.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.
items.t: New EU budget proposal aims at tax gobal tech giants

items.title: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
items.summary: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.

items.summary:
U.N. talks in Geneva have failed to deliver binding rules on autonomous weapons, as humanitarian groups warn that military AI is advancing far faster than diplomacy.

items.summary: The stock market sees its lowest week of 2026. Plus, the magical migration of monarch butterflies. All this and more.

items.title: Denmark says Russia behind plot to kill U.S.-Ukrainian citizen on its soil

items.title: Haitians excited but uneasy as El Salvador troops fight gangs
items.summary:
Foreign combatants in Port-au-Prince welcomed by many after years of gang control but some fear offensive could exacerbate volatile situation

A bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground. But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch.

In 2024, as the surrounding city was almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs, Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played – also fell under criminal control, its dilapidated red and blue stands used as an outpost by fighters working for a gang boss called Izo. Haiti’s national team, the Grenadiers, found itself homeless and was forced to play its World Cup qualifying games abroad.

items.title: China commits to low-carbon electrification and help for others to improve
items.summary:
Exclusive: Countries at Cop31 are being urged to commit to deriving 35% of their energy from electricity by 2035

China is pushing for rapid electrification of its economy using low-carbon energy and will help other countries do the same, a senior member of the Chinese delegation at the Cop31 UN climate summit has said.

Wang Yi, a professor of energy and environment policy at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a senior adviser to China’s government, said: “End-use electrification is a very clear direction. We can follow this direction while making the source of electricity clean. That’s the way to go forward.”

In a discursive press conference from the White House briefing room, Trump also said he would “look into” the report that Iran had been planning to possibly detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington DC, and backed JD Vance over comments the vice-president made blaming Republican midterm losses on the Iran war.

items.title: Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains as AI sell-off dampens Anthropic’s second day of trading
items.summary:
The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout

  • Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?

As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory.

Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.

items.title: ‘Weak and dizzy’: the secretive ICE force-feeding tactics that ended a Cuban father’s hunger strike
items.summary:
Exclusive: Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez says in messages to Guardian from inside Texas facility pain of force-feeding caused him to break strike

The text message that came from inside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention center was stark: “I have spent five days eating regular food. If I don’t eat it, they put the tube in me to feed me.”

A Cuban asylum seeker, Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez, 32, said in messages to the Guardian this month that he was still weak and dizzy after three months without eating, but that he had broken his hunger strike because being force-fed was just too painful.

items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.summary:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.
items.t: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state

items.title: Race to be next UN secretary general exposes divisions among world powers
items.summary:
Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner

The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations.

Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.

items.t: Race to be next UN secretary general exposes divisions among world powers

items.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
items.summary:
The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits

Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.

The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.

items.title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
items.summary:
Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds

One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.

items.t: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN

items.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
items.summary:
A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza

Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

Continue reading...
items.t: Fears grow over US sanctions on ICJ judges ahead of Myanmar genocide ruling
